question: Where are browser/CDP/screenshot/screen interaction, read_image/attachments/render_ui, 3D asset inspect/edit/preview/game-dev helpers, computer/perception/audio/voice capabilities and their CLI/model/tool consumers implemented, wired, tested and documented?

selectedFiles.reason: Complete browser agent entrypoint, default interactionPolicy, required Chrome availability, declared action/observation workflow, tool grants and structured success/failure/partial output consumed by the parent and CLI. Compare the stated policy with the real runtime and parameter path below.

Production browser tool handler: sequencing, browser-use identity check, its action allowlist, recursive diagnose inspection, plan-only ancestry, denial output and browser owner stamp. Compare this effective policy with the shared policy, schema default and generic-agent/SDK call paths.

Real SDK dispatch for read_image, inspect_3d_asset, render_3d_preview, edit_3d_asset and browser_logs; AbortSignal/fileFilter/host-process-view checks, input conversion and trusted browser ownership. Follow this consumer rather than assuming exported helpers are callable from every host.

Complete browser action dispatcher: actual CDP navigation, snapshot, screenshot media, input, state/emulation, tabs, recording, JSON-only PDF, pixel_diff and diagnose execution; unsupported actions, empty captures and caught failures. Trace optional advertised controls and recursive ownership through real helpers.

Browser creation and attachment implementation: pipe launch, WebSocket port fallback, per-run user data, transport selection, target discovery, event routing, registration and rollback when spawn or stop races fail. Generic subprocess/env/sandbox policy is pair09; this slice establishes the actual browser consumer and transport.

Actual browser teardown, stop-versus-spawn markers, transport/socket disposal, child-exit wait, deferred directory cleanup and owner-based reaping. Compare the isolation and cancellation promises with run-end ownership and concurrently active browser sessions.

CDP send/framing, request timeouts, write backpressure, buffer growth/caps, parsed response/event routing and close rejection/cleanup. This is the real action/observation transport, with a separate WebSocket bridge available as an optional edge.

Complete native image read: original-byte media and per-path metadata, supported-format/path/filter checks, initial cancellation, file and total attachment bounds, concurrent I/O, missing/ignored/unsupported/oversize results. Provider vision routing and model content conversion remain pair02.

Production user-message preparation: atomic attachment drain, pending image/text/file selection, image processor invocation, conversation-change cancellation, prompt versus displayed attachment data and resulting MessageContent. Follow the processor and client.run edge in secondary sections.

Image input capability from file and clipboard to CLI store: processing/ready/error states, source provenance, replacement identity, removal during asynchronous work, preserved errors and validate-and-add behavior. Recovery and retry are explicit optional consumer edges.

Complete real render_ui consumer: supported button recognition, theme colors, browser-opening and clipboard services, loading/launch/failure/copy states, stale async generation protection, retained address fallback and tool component registration contract. Compare runtime success output with actual rendered support.

Fixed Blender inspection/import/preview/edit Python scripts and bounded subprocess execution. Inspect actual supported formats, camera/material/wireframe behavior, declarative operation vocabulary, nonzero/Python/spawn/output-limit/timeout/cancellation results. Child environment and generic kill guarantees belong to pair09.

Native 3D inspection and deterministic preview orchestration: project/filter/size checks, built-in versus Blender formats, source hashes and derived metadata cache, render artifacts and source-bound receipts, read_image media projection and failure results. Verify both format coverage and receipt/evidence truth.

Complete bounded .blend mutation capability: exact source hash, conditionalCommit requirement, declarative payload file, attempt-scoped working copy ownership, re-open validation, cancellation, stale/CAS rejection, unknown commit result, retained artifacts, post-commit preview and published mutation receipts. Binary tool semantics belong here; common mutation broker authority is pair06.

Current behavior tests for nested/malformed diagnose, concurrent log/network observation windows, buffer trimming, pipe probe dedup, waiter timeout cleanup, recording-start rollback/retry and concurrent page reconnect. Distinguish synthetic transport assurance from a real Chrome end-to-end test.

Current 3D tests for glTF/GLB/OBJ observations, path/filter rejection, stale mutation before Blender/artifacts, payload file transport, exact payload bounds and rejected-attempt cleanup. Read without launching Blender; distinguish native parser assurance from successful render/edit integration.

Complete Unity/Godot/Unreal/Bevy/Blender preset and job-guidance API: prompt insertion versus executable commands, build/run/test/watch flows, local/native 3D tool suggestions and job/readiness/error/stop recipes. Trace actual slash-command and system-prompt consumers before crediting structured guidance as wired.

Current user-facing policy and capability claims: browser default/read-only ancestry/isolated run cleanup, intentional full-access context, specialist/control-plane edges and the documented 3D discovery/inspect/preview/edit workflow and Blender absence behavior. Treat docs as contracts to compare with current implementation.

searchCoverage.sampling: 18 primary sections across 14 current files, 4805 lines; secondary ranges are optional hypothesis-driven edges and are not inspection credit until the reviewer reads them. This artifact is a picker handoff, not findings or a full-line audit.
searchCoverage.policyContext: Intentional first-party full-access execution and current relaxed/keep policy are established by the parent. Assess actual browser declared/effective policy consistency and opted-in boundaries; do not prescribe general restrictions against that preference.
excluded: No source edits, findings, tests/probes, browser/model/API launches, credential values or private images were used. Only the assigned picker artifact is written.
Pair09 owns generic environment/process/kill/sandbox/approval/egress behavior; browser transport/owner/action-observation wiring is inspected here.
Pair10 owns plugin/MCP provenance/trust/result semantics; MCP audio projection is a necessary observation cross-reference.
Pair02 owns provider/model vision routing and multimodal content conversion; image/media body producers and CLI consumers are inspected here.
Pair06 owns common filesystem mutation broker/receipt authority; the specific binary .blend capability and evidence are inspected here.
Pair07/08 own generic language and indexer behavior; only 3D/engine discovery and consumer edges are selected here.
Historical polyglot plans are context only and excluded from current inventory receipts.
remainingQuestions: Which exact browser actions and declared optional controls are effective for default, explicit read-only, plan-descendant, generic-agent and direct-SDK calls?
Does per-agent browser ownership survive real SDK trust stamping and run-end cleanup during concurrent runs and startup/cancellation races?
Are screenshots/snapshots/diffs/recordings/PDF metadata truthful and usable by their actual model and CLI consumers in empty/error/unsupported media states?
Do attachments retain the capture the user sees through send preparation, stale conversation changes, removal, retry and provider conversion?
Does render_ui success describe actual supported UI on every host, and do opening/copy failure states preserve a useful fallback?
Do all discoverable 3D formats actually inspect/render, and do preview hashes/dimensions bind the exact bytes Blender opened and images emitted?
Are successful, rejected, stale, unknown and post-commit-preview-failed 3D edits and artifact lifetimes reported accurately?
Which game helper exports are actual consumers and which are prompt-only recipes or unwired guidance?
What current desktop/computer/audio/voice paths are callable and tested, as opposed to browser input, image display, protocol fields and historical plans?
